b: Hi. It’s been a while, but I had an interesting experience tonight and felt this was the appropriate place to share it. I’ve been working on losing weight for about two years now and I’ve just recently been able to actually shred some weight. At the beginning of this year, I started at 170 pounds and I’m currently 152 pounds. Very proud of this progress but as a 23 year old 5’4 female, I still have a long way to go.

This evening, I was at a bar with some coworkers who double as friends, and one of my coworkers asked me if I was losing weight or trying to lose weight. I was surprised because I don’t feel like I’ve lost enough weight for it to be noticeable, but also flattered that someone had noticed. I then responded and said I was working on it and that it was exciting it was noticeable. He then responded “why are you trying to lose weight? You’re already tiny. You need to stop.” and in a way it was flattering, but in another way, it didn’t make me feel good. I know I’m not tiny and I know I definitely have at least another 20 pounds that I could lose. but just as I have a fear of being overweight I also have a fear of being unaware of when I look sickly (bc of too much weight loss). I don’t wanna lose too much weight so that I look unhealthy but I also know that I’m not at that point now. How do yall find comfort in your weight loss/know when to stop? I’m not 100% sure what I’m asking for other than your take on the situation, so please feel free to comment.
